notes: CORRECTED 2026-07-31 — plant code field naming IS uniform: every endpoint in this domain takes snake_case `plant_code_id`, and it is declared required=true on every GET. The earlier claim here (that `componentsFromFolder`, `DELETE /diagrams` and the pin endpoint use camelCase `plantCodeId`) was taken from a pasted doc and is WRONG — the live OpenAPI schema declares no `plantCodeId` parameter anywhere in the API, and sending it produced 404/400s. `plantCodeId` remains listed in apiClient.js's PLANT_CODE_KEYS guard, which is harmless: that guard is a shared superset across domains, so an extra key costs nothing.

CORRECTED 2026-07-31 — PATH PARAMS ARE REAL PATH SEGMENTS. The earlier 'path params means query params' resolution recorded here was WRONG against this backend and silently broke six endpoints. The live OpenAPI schema declares these `"in": "path"`, and the query-param forms do not route at all. Evidence (direct curl, dev-token cookie): GET /loadDiagram?diagramId=.. -> 404 {"detail":"Not Found"} vs GET /loadDiagram/{id} -> 200 with the real diagram; DELETE /diagrams?diagram_id=.. -> 405 {"detail":"Method Not Allowed"} vs DELETE /diagrams/{id} -> app-level {"success":false,"message":"Diagram not found"}; GET /generateJob?jobId=.. -> 404 {"detail":"Not Found"} vs GET /generateJob/{jobId} -> app-level "Job not found"; GET /component?component_name=.. -> 404 vs GET /component/{name} -> 200; POST /diagram/pin -> 404 vs POST /diagrams/{id}/pin -> route matches. THE ROUTING TELL: an app-level {success:false,...} body means the route matched and the app rejected the input; a bare {"detail":"Not Found"} means the route does not exist. Use that distinction before ever concluding an endpoint 'works'.

POST /clients/detailedEquipmentSummary/generate's body ({ plant_code_id, items[], provider }) is byte-identical in shape to POST /generate (component generation) — confirmed by the user to be the REAL contract for this endpoint (not a copy-paste doc error), even though the old pre-refactor behavior was a no-payload trigger. The current UI (handleGenerateSummary in useSidebarState.js) has no natural source for `items` for this trigger action, so it currently sends `items: []` with the existing AI-generator `provider` state as a placeholder — flag to product/backend if a real items list is expected here.

POST /generateFromFile is multipart/form-data — plant_code_id is sent as a FormData field (not a query param), per the user's explicit choice to follow the doc's literal grouping (no separate 'Query params:' heading set it apart from the other form fields, unlike componentsFromFolder's plantCodeId which WAS explicitly separated). If the backend 422s with a loc-bearing error pointing at query, move it.

The old contract's GET /clients (workspace list) and client-name-keyed paths (e.g. /clients/{client_name}/detailed-equipment-summary/...) do not exist in the refactored contract at all. Per explicit user decision, the entire 'Workspace Projects' / client-picker UI (useSidebarState.js's activeClient/fetchClients/handleSelectClient state, AiGeneratorTab.jsx's project list) was deleted rather than kept — every endpoint is now scoped by the app's existing global plant selector (useApp().plantCode), not a per-feature workspace list.

RESOLVED (2026-07-31) — the Saved Workflows sidebar (PaletteTab.jsx) always showed 'No saved diagrams'. Root cause: useSidebarState.js's fetchSidebarData mapped over `sidebarData.diagrams` as the BASE array while the envelope was still wrapped (see the unwrap note below), so the base array was always empty and /diagrams's real data was only used for a by-id merge that never ran. GET /diagrams is now the base list. NOTE, correcting an earlier version of this same note: /sidebarData DOES return a `diagrams` key — the claim that it 'only has data.components' came from a truncated doc paste. Live response for plant new123 is `data: { components: [11 items], diagrams: [1 item] }`. Its diagram entries carry only {id, name}, however, whereas GET /diagrams carries id/name/nodes/edges/components/matched_components/created_at/saved_at/updated_at/pinned/pinned_at/is_dashboard — so /diagrams is authoritative for this list and /sidebarData adds nothing to it. The two endpoints are therefore split by responsibility rather than merged: WorkflowContext owns /sidebarData (for its `components` half, which feeds the palette) and useSidebarState owns /diagrams. One call each, no duplication, and no cross-dependency that could let one failure blank the other.

ROOT-CAUSE BUG FOUND & FIXED (2026-07-31) — DOMAIN-WIDE: diagramService.js never unwrapped the {success,message,data} envelope documented above (`responseEnvelope`), unlike every sibling service on a domain with the same envelope (timeseriesService.js, logsService.js, documentsService.js, connectorsService.js, contextService.js, pipelineService.js, schedulerService.js all already have a local `unwrap = (res) => ('data' in res && 'success' in res) ? res.data : res` piped through `.then()`). Every exported function in diagramService.js now has that same unwrap. Concrete symptoms this caused before the fix: (1) WorkflowContext's `listPnidComponents` catalog build did `Array.isArray(data)` against the still-wrapped envelope (never an array) — the equipment palette never showed real component visuals, silently falling back to nothing. (2) useWorkflowCanvas's `loadDiagram` read `data.id/data.nodes/data.edges` off the envelope — every loaded diagram rendered as an empty canvas regardless of what was actually saved. (3) useWorkflowCanvas's `confirmSave` checked `result?.status === 'success' || result?.id` (both undefined on the envelope) — a successful save was never registered: no success feedback, diagramId never set, so clicking Save again created a NEW duplicate diagram instead of updating, and the auto-save debounce effect's `if (!diagramId) return;` gate never opened (auto-save-on-change was permanently dead). (4) useSidebarState's batch-generate-from-connections flow (`onSaveDiagramLocal` -> `result.id`) silently failed to link the freshly saved diagram back into the canvas. One consumer (`handleOpenPreview` in useSidebarState.js) had already manually compensated for the missing unwrap via its own `data?.data` access — that call site was updated to read the now-already-unwrapped array directly (`Array.isArray(data) ? data : []`) so it isn't double-unwrapped. The follow-up flagged here — `handleGenerate`'s `data.code`/`data.items` and `handleBatchGenerate`'s `data.job_id`/`data.items` reading fields absent from the documented shapes — WAS then completed in the same day's second pass: both now read results through a shared `readGeneratedList()` helper that accepts `results` / `successes` / `items`, handleGenerate falls back to GET /component/{name} when no inline `code` comes back, and both call refreshSidebarData() afterwards so newly generated components actually appear in the palette. See the openIssue fields on generateComponents and generateDetailedEquipmentSummary for the two shapes that remain schema-confirmed rather than live-confirmed (invoking them costs real AI generations).

endpoints.name: listComponents
endpoints.description: List all components in the equipment database.
endpoints.note: CONFIRMED live (2026-07-31): `code` is real, complete, renderable TSX source per component — a full React functional component accepting { x, y, scale, status, label, onPointerDown } props, using status-driven fill/stroke colors and an animated status indicator circle. No `viewBox` field is returned — the frontend already derives it itself via SvgParser.js's calculateViewBox() from the parsed markup's x/y/width/height/cx/cy attributes, so no contract gap there. PALETTE SOURCE (final state after two same-day reversals, 2026-07-31): this IS the palette/canvas bootstrap — WorkflowContext.fetchComponents() calls listPnidComponents() eagerly once per plant (an earlier note here claimed the palette had moved to /sidebarData + per-component lazy hydration; that was itself reversed back to the eager bulk approach — see the /component/{name} entry's note, which is the authoritative record of that decision). RENDERING CONSTRAINT (RCA 2026-07-31): every component's TSX roots at a bare <g> element, never <svg>. The client-side SvgParser must therefore sanitize with DOMPurify NAMESPACE: 'http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' — without it, DOMPurify parses the rootless fragment as HTML and its namespace check strips every SVG-only tag, returning an empty string, which rendered ALL components as empty placeholder boxes in both the palette and canvas. Also: DOMPurify blocks SMIL <animate> by default (the status-LED pulse in generated code), so ADD_TAGS: ['animate'] is required to keep those animations.

endpoints.name: loadDiagram
endpoints.description: Load a saved diagram by ID.
endpoints.brokenBefore: GET /loadDiagram?diagramId=.. -> HTTP 404 {"detail":"Not Found"}. This broke the core 'click a saved workflow to open it' flow outright — combined with the missing unwrap, clicking a saved diagram could only ever produce an empty canvas. Corrected form GET /loadDiagram/{id}?plant_code_id=new123 -> HTTP 200 with the real nodes/edges.
endpoints.note: Path renamed from 'load_diagram/{diagram_id}' to 'loadDiagram/{diagramId}' — camelCased, but STILL a real path segment (an earlier version of this note claimed diagramId became a query param; that was wrong, see brokenBefore). CONFIRMED live (2026-07-31) success shape adds components/matched_components/created_at/saved_at/updated_at/pinned/is_dashboard/pinned_at — none of these are currently consumed by useWorkflowCanvas.js's loadDiagram (only id/name/nodes/edges are read); no UI need for them yet, so left unconsumed rather than speculatively wired up. IMPORTANT: the sample node under `data.nodes` has only { id, data: {label, componentType} } — no `position` or `type` (React Flow requires both to place/render a node; without `type` it silently falls back to React Flow's plain default node instead of our IndustrialNode). Per user decision (2026-07-31), useWorkflowCanvas.js's loadDiagram now normalizes every loaded node/edge defensively (auto-grid-layout position + type:'industrial' fallback for nodes missing them; type:'pipe' + default marker/data fallback for edges) rather than assuming the backend always echoes back the full React Flow node shape our own saveDiagram sends.

endpoints.name: saveDiagram
endpoints.description: Create or update a saved diagram.
endpoints.note: Path renamed from 'save_diagram' to 'saveDiagram'. Doc's example only shows the create case (no `id`); the service still passes through an optional `id` field for the update case, matching the prior implementation's create-or-update semantics — not contradicted by the doc, just not shown in its example. CONFIRMED live (2026-07-31) full success response shape matches loadDiagram's (adds components/matched_components/created_at/saved_at/updated_at beyond id/name/nodes/edges). ROOT-CAUSE BUG FOUND & FIXED (2026-07-31): diagramService.js had NO envelope unwrap at all (every other domain service with this same {success,message,data} envelope — timeseriesService.js/logsService.js/documentsService.js/connectorsService.js/contextService.js/pipelineService.js/schedulerService.js — already had a local `unwrap()` piped through `.then()`; this file alone was missing it). Consequence for THIS endpoint specifically: useWorkflowCanvas.js's confirmSave checked `result?.status === 'success' || result?.id` against the still-wrapped envelope, both undefined, so a successful save was never registered — diagramId never got set, the Save button gave no success feedback, clicking Save again created a DUPLICATE diagram instead of updating (id stayed null every time), and the auto-save debounce effect's `if (!diagramId) return;` gate never opened (so auto-save-on-change was permanently dead too). Fixed by adding unwrap() to every real call in diagramService.js and simplifying confirmSave's check to `result?.id` (the `status` field never existed in the real contract).
